description: The University of Strathclyde publishes the raw REFIT electrical load measurements for twenty United Kingdom homes under a distinct DOI. The own record describes aggregate and appliance-level power in watts at eight-second intervals, collected during normal household routines. A modeller can use the series to calibrate appliance demand, load-disaggregation methods or residential demand response in an electricity simulation. Raw observations retain measurement and timestamp issues that the separate cleaned REFIT release addresses. Each house has a CSV series and contextual ReadMe information on appliance assignments; the article describes the acquisition period and sensor changes. This is a small, non-random household sample and should not be treated as a national demand profile. DataCite states CC BY 4.0 for the raw DOI. I read repository metadata and the descriptor without downloading CSV files. The existing catalogue record data-refit-smart-homes-uk covers the related cleaned series, not this raw deposit. A caveat is that raw time stamps and occasional sensor gaps require checking before demand simulation.
